body.p: Favorable reconsideration of this application, as presently amended and in light of the following discussion, is respectfully requested.

Claims 1-20 are currently pending. Claims 1, 5, 15, and 20 have been amended. The changes to the claims are supported by the originally filed specification and claims.1 Thus, no new matter has been added.

In the outstanding Office Action, Claims 1-5, 8, 9, 11-13, and 15-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Publication No. 2016/0129345 to Seok et al. (hereinafter "Seok") in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2021/0008458 to Wang et al. (hereinafter "Wangl"). Claim 6 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Seok in view of Wang1 and U.S. Patent Publication No. 2018/0121086 to Wang et al. (hereinafter "Wang2"). Claim 7 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Seok in view of Wangl, Wang2, and U.S. Patent Publication No. 2019/0303201 to Jiang et al. (hereinafter "Jiang"). Claims 10 and 14 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Seok in view of Wangl and U.S. Publication No. 2018/0304158 to Miyamae et al. (hereinafter "Miyamae").

Applicant and Applicant's representatives thank Examiner Henry for the courtesy of the interview with Applicant's representatives Sean Salimi (80,078) and Johnny Ma (59,976) on October 9, 2024, at which time proposed amendments to Claim 1 were discussed. During the interview, the amendments presently introduced were discussed as distinguishing over the applied references.
Independent Claim 1 is directed to a virtual object control method, comprising: obtaining a skill type of a skill in response to a first touch user operation on a skill control;

displaying, in response to determining that the obtained skill type of the skill is a target skill, a castable region of the skill in a virtual scene according to a position where a controlled virtual
1 See, e.g., [0090]-[0094] and Fig. 6 of corresponding U.S. Publication No. 2022/0032183.
object is located and a casting range of the skill, the target skill being a skill that supports selecting a casting position based on a second
touch user operation;
displaying a casting countdown of the skill in the virtual scene in response to the skill being the target skill; and

controlling, during the casting countdown and in response to the second touch user operation in the castable region, the controlled virtual object to cast the skill at the casting position on which the
second touch user operation is performed.
Regarding the rejection of Claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 103, it is respectfully submitted

that Seok and Wang1 fail to disclose "controlling, during the casting countdown and in response to the second touch user operation in the castable region, the controlled virtual object to cast the skill at the casting position on which the second touch user operation is performed," as discussed during the interview. Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that Claim 1 (and all associated dependent claims) patentably defines over Seok and Wang1.
Independent Claims 15 and 20, although differing in scope and/or statutory class

patentably define over Seok and Wang1 at least for reasons analogous to the reasons stated above for the patentability of Claim 1. Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that Claims 15 and 20 patentably define over Seok and Wang1.
Regarding the rejections of Claims 6, 7, 10, and 14 under 35 U.S.C. § 103, it is

respectfully submitted that Claims 6, 7, 10, and 14 patentably define over Seok and Wang1 at least for the reasons stated above for the patentability of Claim 1, from which Claims 6, 7, 10,and 14 depend. Further, the Office Action does not cite Wang2, Jiang, and Miyamae for suchteachings. Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that Claims 6, 7, 10, and 14 patentablydefine over Seok, Wangl, Wang2, Jiang, and Miyamae.

If for any reason the Examiner feels the application is not now in condition for allowance, it is respectfully requested that the Examiner contact the undersigned practitioner to arrange for an interview to expedite the disposition of this case.

If this communication is filed after the shortened statutory time period had elapsed and no separate Petition is enclosed, Applicant hereby petitions, under 37 C.F.R. § 1.136(a), to extend the time for filing a response to the outstanding Office Action by the number of months

necessary to avoid abandonment under 37 C.F.R. § 1.135. Please charge any such fee, or any other fee due under 37 C.F.R. § 1.17, to our Deposit Account No. 01-2300, under 043381.00516, from which the undersigned is authorized to draw.
